title: T1593 — Search Open Websites/Domains
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Search Open Websites/Domains with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram of the T1593 technique: an attacker with a normal web browser researches the fictional company Acme Logistics through open websites such as search engines, social media and code repositories, builds a targeting dossier, while the company security team sees no events in their own logs. A written version of all eight steps follows below the diagram.

steps.title: Choose the target
steps.caption: The attacker picks Acme Logistics and opens a normal web browser. Nothing touches Acme's systems yet.
steps.defender: No events exist in any Acme log. There is nothing to alert on, because no Acme system is involved.

fields.detail: The attacker picks Acme Logistics and opens a normal web browser. Nothing touches Acme's systems yet

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Query search engines
steps.caption: Searches for news about Acme reveal new offices, customers and a merger. The attacker notes who leads what.
steps.defender: Search engines log the queries, not Acme. The company has no way to see them.

steps.title: Crawl the public website
steps.caption: The careers page lists jobs that mention Kubernetes and a specific ERP. Press releases name partner companies.
steps.defender: The web server sees a normal visitor. Nothing separates research from any other reader.

steps.title: Scan social profiles
steps.caption: Employee profiles give names, roles and skills. A photo shows an office with visible screens and badges.
steps.defender: The platform logs this activity. Acme sees nothing unless staff report a suspicious profile.

steps.title: Search code repositories
steps.caption: A search for Acme's domain finds an employee's small public project with internal hostnames in a config file.
steps.defender: If a secret had been published, the code host's secret scanning could fire an alert. Here it is only a hostname, so nothing fires.

steps.title: Build the dossier
steps.caption: The attacker merges everything: people and roles, the real tech stack, one leaked hostname, and possible ways in.
steps.defender: The dossier lives on the attacker's side. Acme cannot see it or delete it.

steps.title: The SOC sees nothing
steps.caption: Acme's dashboards stay empty through the whole research phase. Reconnaissance happened entirely outside.
steps.defender: This is normal for T1593. Visibility must come from external monitoring: brand alerts, exposure scans, leak reports.

steps.title: The outcome
steps.caption: The attacker drafts a tailored lure for people in the dossier. Acme will see it only when the phishing email arrives.
steps.defender: The best defense happened earlier: shrink the public footprint so the dossier is thin. Next best: catch the lure at the mail gateway.
